issue.title: Bug: LRH upstream neighbors route-churn when using existing t2 j2 templates

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

While using the existing j2 templates for lrh (lrh-core.j2 -> t2-leaf.j2, lrh-leaf.j2 -> t2-core.j2), we are experiencing route churcning on upstream neighbors (FRH and URH)

### Steps to Reproduce

Perform `redeploy-topo` + `deploy-mg` for LRH device, wait a while for route churn to happen (may be more common after link flap)

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Route churn shouldn't happen

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Prevent route churning on upstream neighbors on LRH topologies
#### How did you do it?
Remove `allowas-in` from the EOS neighbor configurations, in `lrh-core.j2` template file (`lrh-core.j2` was originally symlinked to `t2-leaf.j2` as a template but is not dependent on the file itself. For LRH specific purposes, we decided to fork from [`t2-leaf.j2`](https://github.com/Javier-Tan/sonic-mgmt/blob/3059bd1d4939f63502253bf3ae59057df18f4d47/ansible/roles/eos/templates/t2-leaf.j2#L128) and remove `allowas-in` config)
#### How did you verify/test it?
Removed `allowas-in` from EOS neighbors during route churn, saw it stop. Tested for 24h stability
